organization.name: Customer (name not supplied)

sources.title: Expense reimbursement checklist
sources.note: Three-item checklist supplied in chat on 2026-09-21. No org chart, no service levels and no policy on limits were supplied.

groups.name: Line managers
groups.purpose: Approve the expense claims of the employees who report to them (checklist item b). Fallback owner of the approval when the approving manager named in the claim cannot be assigned per case.

flags.detail: The checklist says «manager» without an org chart; which managers approve, and for whom, is unknown. Membership must come from the customer (decision D2).

A manager who submits a claim must not approve it. The design assigns the approval to the manager named in the claim (field `manager`), with this group as fallback; the customer must confirm the rule for managers' own claims (decision D3).

groups.name: Finance
groups.purpose: Pay approved expense claims within the month and record the payment evidence (checklist item c).

flags.detail: «Finance» is named as a department; no members, lead or process owner were supplied (decision D1 and D6).

workflows.name: Expense reimbursement

grants.reason: Item (a) says the employee submits receipts; read as any employee of the organization may open a claim for their own expenses.

access.note: No `edit` grant is declared because the checklist names no process owner (decision D1). Finance and line managers see the claims that carry their actions without a grant; a `view` grant to Finance (every claim, for month-end planning) is an open question (D7), not proposed from the assignment alone.

accessReview.question: Does Finance need to see every claim, including those not yet approved, to plan the month's payment run? If yes, add group:finance at level view with this checklist item as the source.

actions.name: Submit the expense receipts
evidence: Every receipt attached to the claim as a file (legible scan or photo)
Fields claim_amount, expense_period, expense_category, business_purpose, receipt_count and manager filled

folded.summary: Handing the claim to the manager is the completion of this action; the approval is activated by sequencing, not by a separate hand-off step.

actions.name: Decide on the expense claim
evidence: Decision recorded on the claim: Approve, Return for correction or Reject
A comment with the reason is mandatory on Return for correction and Reject

folded.summary: The employee learns the outcome from the claim itself (creator sees the case); no separate notification action is emitted.

actions.name: Pay the approved reimbursement
evidence: Fields paid_amount, payment_date and payment_reference filled
Proof of payment (bank transfer confirmation or cash voucher) attached

setupNotes: Owners: `approve_claim` is intended for the manager the claimant names in the case field `manager`; the product cannot assign from a case field, so the fallback group Line managers (a role group) is the configured owner and the case owner is set manually per claim until the customer confirms the routing (decision D2).
Groups Line managers and Finance have no members: the customer supplied no org chart. Add members in Provia before the pilot.

The YAML omits `assignee` on `approve_claim` and `pay_claim` because the destination group ids are unknown; set them in Provia after creating the groups, or run resolve-workflow-refs.mjs once receipts exist.

No `due` is set on any action: the checklist gives no service level for submission or approval, and «within the month» (item c) is a calendar deadline the contract's offset-based `due` cannot express. Configure the payment deadline per case or agree an offset (decisions D4 and D5).

The intake form `expense-claim-intake` is a recommendation for self-service starts; forms are not carried by YAML and must be created and linked in Provia. Without it, employees start the claim from the manual trigger and fill the fields in `submit_claim`.
The rejection and return-for-correction branches are proposed, not in the checklist (decision D8).
Expense categories in `expense_category` are a proposed starting list, not customer policy; adjust to the customer's policy on limits once it exists (decision D9).
Claimants' bank details are not stored in Provia; Finance pays from the payroll or accounting system of record (decision D6).

forms.title: Expense claim
forms.respondents: Internal: any signed-in employee, for their own expenses.
forms.access: Internal form behind Provia sign-in. No anonymous or external link. Submitting on behalf of another employee is not designed (open question in the form specification).

fields.label: Total amount claimed (Kz)
fields.helpText: Sum of all attached receipts, in kwanzas.

fields.label: Expense period
fields.helpText: The dates or month the receipts cover, for example «8–12 September 2026».

fields.label: Business purpose
fields.helpText: What the expense was for and which work it supported.

fields.label: Approving manager
fields.helpText: Your line manager. The claim is routed to this person for approval.

fields.label: Receipts
fields.helpText: Attach every receipt (PDF, JPG or PNG). One file per receipt or one combined PDF.

uploads.maxSizeNote: Use the tenant's default file limit; no customer requirement was supplied.
uploads.reason: The receipts are the only evidence of the expense (checklist item a).

forms.confirmation: Your expense claim {{reference}} was recorded and sent to your manager for approval. You can follow it in Provia; Finance pays approved claims within the month.
forms.responsePolicy: One submission creates one claim; values map to the case fields listed in mapsTo. Receipts stay attached to the case as files.
testing: Submit a claim as a test employee and confirm the case opens with the seven mapped values and the attached files.
Confirm the selected manager can see the claim and the decision action.
Confirm an employee cannot see another employee's claim (no view grant).

decisions.question: Who owns the expense reimbursement process (the person or group that will hold the `edit` grant, sign off the design and answer the other decisions)? No process owner is named in the checklist.

Which manager approves each claim: the claimant's direct line manager, a department head, or any member of a managers group? Provia cannot route by the requester's manager automatically; the design has the claimant name the approving manager in the field `manager` and keeps the group Line managers as fallback. The customer must supply the org chart or the list of approving managers.
Segregation: who approves a claim submitted by a manager, and is a claimant ever allowed to approve their own claim? The checklist does not say.

Service levels: how many workdays does the employee have to complete a returned claim, and how many does the manager have to decide? None were supplied, so `due` is unset on `submit_claim` and `approve_claim`.

«Finance pays within the month»: within the calendar month of approval, of submission, or of the expense? And is a fixed offset acceptable instead (for example 10 workdays after approval) so the deadline can be configured as `due`? Until answered, the payment deadline is set manually per claim.

Where does Finance take the claimant's bank details from (payroll, accounting system, HR file), and by which means are reimbursements paid (bank transfer, cash, payroll)? This decides whether an Employee entity type is needed in Provia; the design keeps bank details out of Provia.

Does Finance need to see every claim (a `view` grant on the workflow) to plan the monthly payment run, or only the claims that reach the payment action? The checklist does not say; no view grant is proposed.

The checklist has no rejection or correction path. The design proposes three outcomes for the manager: Approve, Return for correction (back to the employee) and Reject (closes the claim). Confirm or change.

Policy on limits: maximum amounts per claim or category, eligible expense categories, receipt requirements (original vs copy, minimum information) and what happens above a manager's authority. No policy exists; the decision brief tells the manager to apply the policy in force and to return the claim when unsure. Provide the policy or confirm that none applies for the pilot.

Language of the deliverable: the project was written in English as requested. Confirm whether the action names, briefs and form labels shown to employees in Angola should be delivered in pt-AO before publication.
